fields.sample_size: 213 small municipalities (population up to 50,000; 95.5% of the 223 municipalities of Paraiba state, northeast Brazil; about 42% predominantly rural in the 2010 census); secondary data: IBGE 2010 census, MUNIC 2017, Atlas Esgoto 2017 and the SUS health system 2010-2014; index built with multivariate standardisation and weighting and validated with GIS mapping
fields.effect_measure: composite Human Vulnerability Index to the Insufficiency of Basic Sanitation (IVHIS: risk, susceptibility and adaptive-capacity dimensions, IPCC framework) scored 0 to 1 per municipality; descriptive distribution by mesoregion; no inferential effect estimate
fields.effect_estimate: About 62% of the 213 municipalities had a medium risk score; 26 municipalities had the highest sanitation inadequacy scores, concentrated in the Sertao (42.3%) and the Agreste (34.6%) mesoregions, with inadequate sewage disposal the main driver of risk in 11 Sertao municipalities; the Agreste Paraibano shows high vulnerability from economic, health and socio-demographic characteristics, and the index shows a geographic influence of large urban centres on surrounding small municipalities. The authors conclude that vulnerability indicates inequity and social inequality and that indices can target public policies; institutional variables are only one input (for example MUNIC data on municipal sanitation management).
fields.section: Full text (Portuguese with English and Spanish abstracts, 31 pages): Introduction; Method (framework, data, standardisation, weighting, validation); Results (risk, susceptibility, adaptive capacity, IVHIS maps); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Method sections; Results on the 213 municipalities and mesoregions; Conclusions; Rev. Gest. Amb. Sustent. 13(1):e25071

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a quantitative index-construction and validation study for 213 small municipalities of Paraiba, Brazil, using census and administrative data; read in full text 2026-10-04. No legal or administrative exposure is tested.
pdf_note: Revista de Gestao Ambiental e Sustentabilidade 13(1):e25071, Portuguese, 31 pages scanned (method, results and conclusion sections read; the weighting tables were not read)
notes: FIT FLAG: an index of sanitation vulnerability from secondary data; the institutional element is a few MUNIC management variables and no legal factor is examined (criterion 2 thin). Candidate for the criterion-2 scope check.
